review.notes: Capitalized "Keeper" is taken as a common noun (the capitalized-common-noun default), so the individual-subject Member and the agent-nominalization capability both follow: the nominalization is the clause's copular predicate, which is one of the two fixed places the (can keep) atom fires. If "Keeper" is instead an office/title rather than "one who keeps", the definitional (can keep) atom would over-commit, but the item supplies no cue for that reading.
